title: Meet the queen
objectives: Understand the queen combines rook and bishop movement

steps.text: The queen is the most powerful piece. She moves like a rook and a bishop combined — straight lines and diagonals, any distance.

steps.prompt: Move the queen along any straight line or diagonal, as far as it can go.

hints.text: The queen can move in any straight or diagonal direction — pick one and go as far as possible.
Straight lines and diagonals are both open to her.
The queen can slide straight up from e4 to e8.

feedback.default: The queen moves in straight lines or diagonals only — not like a knight.

steps.successExplanation: That's a legal queen move — any straight line or diagonal, any distance, is open to her.

steps.prompt: Capture the black knight on b1 with your queen, sliding along the diagonal.

hints.text: The queen captures the way she moves — find the diagonal that reaches the knight.
The knight sits on the same diagonal as your queen.
The queen captures on b1 — straight down the e4-b1 diagonal.

feedback.default: Look for a straight line or diagonal from the queen's square that reaches the knight, with nothing else in the way.

steps.successExplanation: Qxb1 captures the knight. The e4-b1 diagonal was completely open, so the queen could slide the whole way.

steps.prompt: Move the queen as far as she can go up the e-file — her own pawn stops her early.

hints.text: The queen can't move through or capture her own pieces — she stops right before them.
There's a white pawn on e6, two squares up.
The farthest she can go up the e-file is here.
The queen can reach e5, but no further — her own pawn on e6 blocks the rest of the file.

feedback.default: The queen can't land on or move past a square her own piece occupies. Up the e-file, that own pawn on e6 stops her at e5.

steps.successExplanation: Right — the queen isn't blocked by distance, only by pieces in her path. Her own pawn on e6 means e5 is as far as she can go that direction.

steps.prompt: A queen can capture her own pawn if that's the only way to get past it.

feedback.default: No piece can ever capture a piece on its own side — friendly pieces block movement, they're never valid targets.

steps.successExplanation: Right — a queen simply cannot move onto or through a square her own piece occupies, no exceptions.
